title: Bias a diode at one milliamp
story: Small-signal diodes are usually characterised at about 1 mA. Your bench supply gives 5 V. Pick the resistor that sets the diode near 1 mA, so its voltage lands in the range the diode equation predicts for that current.
hints: The diode will sit somewhere near 0.65 V, so the resistor sees about 5 - 0.65 V.
I = (5 - 0.65) / R. Which resistor gives about 1 mA?
Ten times more current costs only about 60 mV more diode voltage.
